learningObjectives.title: Rates of change and compound measures

questions.q: Written in its simplest form, the ratio 12 : 18 is:
questions.explain: Divide both parts by the highest common factor, 6, to give 2 : 3.

questions.q: £60 is shared between two people in the ratio 2 : 3. How much does each person receive?
questions.explain: There are 5 parts, so one part is £12, giving 2 × £12 = £24 and 3 × £12 = £36.

questions.q: What does the ratio 3 : 5 tell you about two quantities?
options: For every 3 parts of the first there are 5 parts of the second
The first quantity is 3 and the second is 5
The first quantity is 5 more than the second
The two quantities add up to 8
questions.explain: A ratio compares the relative sizes of quantities in matching parts, not their absolute values.

questions.q: A recipe for 4 people uses 200 g of flour. Keeping the amounts in proportion, how much flour is needed for 6 people?
questions.explain: Flour per person is 200 ÷ 4 = 50 g, so 6 people need 6 × 50 = 300 g.

questions.q: Two lengths are in the ratio 2 : 3. What fraction of the total length is the shorter length?
questions.explain: The total is 2 + 3 = 5 parts, so the shorter length is 2 out of 5, i.e. 2/5.

questions.q: If y is directly proportional to x, which equation represents this relationship (k is a constant)?
questions.explain: Direct proportion means y = kx, where k is the constant of proportionality.

questions.q: If y is inversely proportional to x, which equation represents this relationship (k is a constant)?
questions.explain: Inverse proportion means the product xy is constant, so y = k/x.

questions.q: The graph of two quantities in direct proportion is:
options: A straight line through the origin
A straight line crossing the y-axis above zero
questions.explain: y = kx gives a straight line of gradient k passing through (0, 0).

questions.q: y is directly proportional to x. When x = 3, y = 12. What is y when x = 5?
If y is inversely proportional to x, what happens to y when x is doubled?
questions.explain: With y = k/x, doubling x divides y by 2, so y is halved.

questions.q: Which formula correctly links speed, distance and time?
questions.explain: Average speed is the distance travelled divided by the time taken.

questions.q: Which formula defines density?
questions.explain: Density is mass per unit volume, so density = mass ÷ volume.

questions.q: Which formula defines pressure?
questions.explain: Pressure is the force applied per unit area, so pressure = force ÷ area.

questions.q: A speed is measured in metres per second (m/s). This tells you it is:
options: A rate showing distance travelled each second
questions.explain: A compound unit like m/s expresses one quantity per unit of another — here, metres for each second.

questions.q: An object has a mass of 300 g and a volume of 60 cm³. What is its density?
questions.explain: Density = mass ÷ volume = 300 ÷ 60 = 5 g/cm³.

questions.q: Given speed and time, how do you find the distance travelled?
questions.explain: Rearranging speed = distance ÷ time gives distance = speed × time.

questions.q: Compound interest differs from simple interest because:
options: Interest is earned on the previous interest as well as the original amount
Interest is only ever calculated on the original amount
No interest is added after the first year
The interest rate falls each year
questions.explain: With compound interest each year's interest is added on, so future interest is calculated on the growing total.

questions.q: Which single multiplier represents an increase of 5%?
questions.explain: A 5% increase multiplies by 100% + 5% = 105% = 1.05.

questions.q: A car loses 10% of its value each year. Which multiplier models one year of this depreciation?
questions.explain: A 10% decrease leaves 90% of the value, so you multiply by 0.9.

questions.q: £2000 is invested at 5% compound interest per year. What is it worth after 2 years?
